record.original_question: Let E_n be an n-dimensional normed space having the b-extension property, meaning that every operator T in L(Y,E_n) defined on a subspace Y of E_n extends to an operator on all of E_n with norm at most b||T||. Must the Banach-Mazur distance from E_n to either l_2^n or c_0^n stay uniformly bounded, i.e. is sup_n min{d(E_n,l_2^n), d(E_n,c_0^n)} finite?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a Banach space $X$ and constant $1\le b<\infty$, say that $X$ has the $b$-extension property if for every subspace $Y\subseteq X$ and every bounded linear operator $T\in L(Y,X)$ there exists an extension $\widetilde T\in L(X,X)$ with $\widetilde T\!\restriction_Y = T$ and $\|\widetilde T\|\le b\,\|T\|$.

For $n\in\mathbb N$, let $\ell_2^n$ denote $n$-dimensional Hilbert space and $c_0^n=\ell_\infty^n$ denote $\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm. For finite-dimensional normed spaces $X,Z$ of the same dimension, let
$$d(X,Z)=\inf\{\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\|:T:X\to Z\ \text{linear isomorphism}\}$$
be the Banach–Mazur distance.

Fix $1\le b<\infty$. Suppose that for each $n\in\mathbb N$, $E_n$ is an $n$-dimensional normed space having the $b$-extension property. Must
$$\sup_{n\in\mathbb N}\,\min\bigl\{d(E_n,\ell_2^n),\,d(E_n,c_0^n)\bigr\}<\infty\ ?$$
